assemblies.name: Batch Motor Build
assemblies.description: Builds all four belt-drive motors (Y-Left, Y-Right, Z-Back, Z-Front) in one production-line session. Manual §4 (pulley) and §5 (motor holder + screws + drill-tighten + dangle test). X-Axis motor stays in assembly_d3d_x_axis_bench.
assemblies.learningFocus: Production-line motor assembly: pulley pop check, motor-holder nut bedding, belt-in-channel toothed-side-inward, drill-tighten on lowest torque, dangle-test verification.

partGroups.name: Batch Motor Build (all 4 axes)
partGroups.description: Production-line motor assembly: build all four belt-drive motors (Y-Left, Y-Right, Z-Back, Z-Front) in parallel from manual §4-§5. Mirrors batch_carriage_build and batch_idler_build.
partGroups.milestoneMessage: All four motor units assembled with belts in channels.

steps.name: Lay out 4 motors and motor-holder hardware
steps.instructionText: Lay out the 4 stepper motors (Y-Left, Y-Right, Z-Back, Z-Front), 8 motor-holder half-pieces, 4 GT2 pulleys with set screws, 4 GT2 belts, 16 M3x25 motor screws, 12 M6 hex nuts, and 12 M6x18 holder bolts on your workbench. Group by axis.

steps.name: Clean excess plastic from motor holder holes
steps.instructionText: Use a 6 mm drill bit (or box cutter) to thresh out plastic covering the bolt holes on every motor-holder half. Each half should have clean M6 holes plus a recessed channel for the GT2 belt.

steps.name: QC: verify all motor-holder holes are clean
steps.instructionText: Verify each motor-holder half has clean M6x18 bolt holes, clear M3x25 motor-screw holes, and a clean belt channel. Plastic flash here will prevent the motor from seating.

steps.name: Motor 1 (Y-Left): mount pulley on motor shaft
steps.instructionText: Place the GT2 pulley on the Y-Left motor shaft using the thin spacer to keep the pulley off the housing. Tighten the first set screw with an Allen key.

steps.name: Motor 1: lock pulley set screw until pop
steps.instructionText: Remove the spacer. Tighten the second set screw as firmly as possible. A soft "pop" means the screw is fully seated. Whether or not you hear it, tighten as hard as you can — the belt pulls 20 lbs and the screw cannot slip.

steps.name: Motor 1: load motor-holder half with 3 nuts
steps.instructionText: Lay one motor-holder half-piece flat with the rectangular belt channel away from you. Drop 3 M6 hex nuts into the embedded slots. Per manual §5.1.

steps.name: Motor 1: insert belt in motor-holder channel
steps.instructionText: Lay the GT2 belt in the holder channel with the toothed side facing INWARD (toward the motor pulley). Per manual §5.2.

steps.name: Motor 1: close motor-holder halves
steps.instructionText: Press the second motor-holder half against the first, trapping the belt and nuts. Halves should align flush. Per manual §5.3.

steps.name: Motor 1: confirm belt runs smooth on pulley
steps.instructionText: Hold the motor against the holder and pull the belt gently. Belt should glide smoothly on the pulley with no rub. If it rubs, reseat the belt in the channel.

steps.name: Motor 1: attach motor with 4× M3x25 screws
steps.instructionText: Insert the first M3x25 screw and tighten it ¾ tight with a screwdriver — leaves slight flexibility. Insert the 3 remaining M3x25 screws somewhat loose. Per manual §5.4.

steps.name: Motor 1: insert 3× M6x18 holder bolts
steps.instructionText: Insert 3 M6x18 bolts into the remaining motor-holder holes, threading each into its embedded nut. Hand-snug; the next step uses the drill. Per manual §5.4-cont.

steps.name: Motor 1: drill-tighten holder M6x18 bolts
steps.instructionText: Tighten each of the 3 motor-holder M6x18 bolts into its embedded nut using the electric drill on its lowest torque setting. The motor holder is now fully clamped.

steps.name: Motor 1: dangle test
steps.instructionText: Hold the assembled motor unit by the belt — it should hang freely from the holder without the motor slipping out. Per manual §5.5.
